headline: 138 women MPs targeted by deepfake porn sites across Europe, new research shows
summary: New research reveals 138 women Members of Parliament from 22 EU countries have been targeted by sexually explicit deepfake websites, with women 33 times more likely to be victims than men.
details: New research by Benjamin Shultz, published by Agora Digitale Transformation, reveals that at least 138 women Members of Parliament from 22 European Union countries have been targeted by harmful deepfake pornography websites. Women MPs are 33 times more likely to be included on these sites than their male counterparts.

The abuse ranges from explicit videos featuring their likeness to disturbing database-like entries with names and photos, often linking directly to deepfake creation tools. Some pages even include sections "rating" women's bodies.

Politicians from Germany, the Netherlands, Italy, and France were most frequently targeted, with more senior figures facing higher risks. Dutch MP Suzanne Kröger called the findings "deeply disturbing," highlighting the broader trend of online hate against women in public life.

Lawmakers and researchers warn that such deepfake abuse can severely damage democratic practices and create a "chilling effect," discouraging women and girls from pursuing public office. It inflicts real psychological and reputational harm.

Since deepfakes emerged in late 2017, the technology has become increasingly accessible and realistic. Millions of nonconsensual AI images and videos have been created, predominantly by men, to harass, intimidate, or blackmail women and girls.

headline: College student Maddie Kowalski exploited on camera, video went viral, leading to severe online harassment
summary: A compilation of nonconsensual intimate videos featuring Maddie Kowalski was posted on X, went viral, and led to nearly a year of intense online harassment for her and her family.
details: Maddie Kowalski, a University of Florida sophomore, discovered a nude image of her circulating on Snapchat and YikYak. The situation escalated when a video compilation of nonconsensual intimate clips was posted on X by an anonymous account, quickly going viral.

The video included clips taken at a fraternity house and during a separate sexual encounter when Kowalski was heavily intoxicated. She states she did not consent to being filmed or having the content shared publicly.

The anonymous X account, @SteveCumfull, not only posted the video but also created a cryptocurrency token with Kowalski's name, appearing to profit from her exploitation. This turned a campus rumor into a national story.

For nearly a year, Kowalski and her family have endured relentless online harassment. Anonymous individuals posted her personal information, called her parents with disturbing claims, and even encouraged her to commit suicide.
caption:

For nearly a year, Kowalski and her family have endured relentless online harassment. Anonymous individuals posted her personal information, called her parents with disturbing claims, and even encouraged her to commit suicide.
